chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, and Muhammad ibn Ismail, from Al-Fadl ibn Shazan, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Muawiya ibn Ammar, who said:
I said to Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him): 'The slave sees the hair and the leg of his mistress.' He (peace be upon him) said: 'There is no problem.'

key_terms.لَا بَأْسَ: There is no problem / It is permissible

ai.seo_question: Is it permissible for a slave to look at his mistress's hair and legs?
ai.summary: Recorded in al-Kafi by Shaykh al-Kulayni, this hadith from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies the specific boundaries of modesty within the master-slave relationship, distinguishing it from the stricter rules applied to free women. The ruling of 'la ba'sa' (no harm) indicates that the hair and legs of the mawlati are not considered awrah in this specific context, reflecting the practical legal realities of the time. This narration is foundational in Shia fiqh for understanding the nuances of gaze and modesty relative to social status and marital availability.

en.hubeali: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father and Muhammad Bin Ismail, from Al Fazl Bin Shazaan, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Muawiya Bin Ammar who said,
‘I said to Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup>, ‘The slave sees the hair and the leg of his mistress’. He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘There is no problem’.
en.sarwar: 3. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father and Muhammad ibn ‘Isma’il has narrated from al-Fadl ibn Shadhan from ibn abu ‘Umayr from Mu‘awiyah ibn ‘Ammar who has said the following: “
I once asked abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, about a slave’s looking at the hairs and leg of his mistress. He (the Imam) said, ‘It is not unlawful.’”
